official_questions.stem: One of the following is not a constitutional agency :

statements.t: The Inter-State Council is a constitutional agency.
The Inter-State Commerce Commission is a constitutional agency.

official_questions.stem: What would be the consequence if the State Governments fail to comply with the directions of the Central Government with regard to the exercise of their Administrative Power?
options: The President can send Centre Reserve Police Force for the implementation of directions.
The President can declare a Constitutional Emergency in the State and assume all the powers of the state governments.
The President can declare a National Emergency convert the Federal structure into a unitary one.
official_questions.key: The President can declare a Constitutional Emergency in the State and assume all the powers of the state governments.
official_questions.core_fact: If a State fails to comply with Union directions (Arts 256, 257), the President may hold that its constitutional machinery has failed (Art 365) and impose President's Rule (Art 356).

statements.t: If State Governments fail to comply with Union directions, The President can send Centre Reserve Police Force for the implementation of directions.
statements.d: The President can send Centre Reserve Police Force for the implementation of directions

statements.t: If State Governments fail to comply with Union directions, The President can declare a Constitutional Emergency in the State and assume all the powers of the state governments.
statements.d: The President can declare a Constitutional Emergency in the State and assume all the powers of the state governments

statements.t: If State Governments fail to comply with Union directions, The President can declare a National Emergency convert the Federal structure into a unitary one.
statements.d: The President can declare a National Emergency convert the Federal structure into a unitary one

statements.t: If State Governments fail to comply with Union directions, None of the given options.

official_questions.rule: Non-compliance with directions -> Art 365 -> Art 356 (not 352).

official_questions.stem: Where there is conflict between the Concurrent List and the State List
options: Matter will be referred to the speaker of Lok Sabha
Matter will be referred to the President
official_questions.core_fact: Art 246 makes Parliament's power over List I and III prevail ('notwithstanding') over States' List II power; the key says Concurrent prevails over State List.

statements.t: Where there is conflict between the Concurrent List and the State List, Matter will be referred to the speaker of Lok Sabha.
statements.d: Matter will be referred to the speaker of Lok Sabha

statements.t: Where there is conflict between the Concurrent List and the State List, Matter will be referred to the President.
statements.d: Matter will be referred to the President

statements.t: Where there is conflict between the Concurrent List and the State List, Concurrent List shall prevail.
Where there is conflict between the Concurrent List and the State List, State List shall prevail.

official_questions.rule: Lists hierarchy (Art 246): Union > Concurrent > State; repugnancy between laws (Art 254) is separate.

official_questions.stem: Indian Parliament passes legislations subject to the following limitations and prohibitions
official_questions.core_fact: Parliament's law-making is limited by the Constitution: distribution of powers (Seventh Schedule), Fundamental Rights and other provisions.

statements.t: Indian Parliament passes legislation subject to limitations of Constitutionof UNO.
Indian Parliament passes legislation subject to limitations of Conventions of the country.
Indian Parliament passes legislation subject to limitations of Distribution of powers.
Indian Parliament passes legislation subject to limitations of Public opinion.

official_questions.rule: Indian Parliament is not sovereign like Britain's: federalism, FRs, judicial review limit it.

official_questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a Constitutional Body?
official_questions.core_fact: In 2017 NCSC (Art 338), NCST (Art 338A) and the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (Art 350B) were constitutional; NCBC was statutory (1993 Act) until the 102nd Amendment (2018).

The National Commission for Schedule Tribes is a Constitutional Body.
The National Commission for Backward Classes is a Constitutional Body.
The Special officer for linguistic minorities is a Constitutional Body.

official_questions.rule: Time-stamp: NCBC statutory 1993-2018, constitutional (338B) since 2018.
official_questions.key_note: Time-sensitive: correct for 2017; NCBC became constitutional (Art 338B) by the 102nd Amendment in 2018.

official_questions.stem: Regarding the Comptroller and Auditor General, out of the given below, choose the wrong answer.
options: Comptroller and Auditor General controls the entire financial system of the country related to the Union government only
The term of office of the Comptroller and Auditor General shall be 6 years
Comptroller and Auditor General vacates the office upon attaining the age of 65 years even without completing 6 years term
Comptroller and Auditor General's salary shall be equal to that of judge of Supreme Court
official_questions.key: Comptroller and Auditor General controls the entire financial system of the country related to the Union government only
official_questions.core_fact: CAG audits Union and State accounts (not only Union) and has no control over release of funds; term 6 years or 65; salary equal to an SC judge.

statements.t: Regarding the CAG: Comptroller and Auditor General controls the entire financial system of the country related to the Union government only.
statements.d: Comptroller and Auditor General controls the entire financial system of the country related to the Union government only
statements.fact: CAG is auditor of both Union and States.

statements.t: Regarding the CAG: The term of office of the Comptroller and Auditor General shall be 6 years.
statements.d: The term of office of the Comptroller and Auditor General shall be 6 years

statements.t: Regarding the CAG: Comptroller and Auditor General vacates the office upon attaining the age of 65 years even without completing 6 years term.
statements.d: Comptroller and Auditor General vacates the office upon attaining the age of 65 years even without completing 6 years term

statements.t: Regarding the CAG: Comptroller and Auditor General's salary shall be equal to that of judge of Supreme Court.
statements.d: Comptroller and Auditor General's salary shall be equal to that of judge of Supreme Court

official_questions.rule: CAG: Union + States audit; 6 years/65; removable like an SC judge.

official_questions.stem: Regarding the National Emergency all following statements are correct, except that the President can
options: Reduce the transfer of Finances from Centre to States
Cancel the transfer of Finances from the Centre to States
National Emergency may be imposed for entire Nation or a part of India
Increase the transfer of Finances from Centre to States
official_questions.key: Increase the transfer of Finances from Centre to States
official_questions.core_fact: During a National Emergency the President can modify (reduce or cancel) transfers of finances to the States (Art 354); emergency may cover whole or part of India (42nd Amendment).

statements.t: During a National Emergency the President can Reduce the transfer of Finances from Centre to States.
statements.d: Reduce the transfer of Finances from Centre to States

statements.t: During a National Emergency the President can Cancel the transfer of Finances from the Centre to States.
statements.d: Cancel the transfer of Finances from the Centre to States

statements.t: During a National Emergency the President can impose National Emergency for the entire Nation or a part of India.
statements.d: impose National Emergency for the entire Nation or a part of India

statements.t: During a National Emergency the President can Increase the transfer of Finances from Centre to States.
statements.d: Increase the transfer of Finances from Centre to States
statements.fact: Transfers can be reduced or cancelled.

official_questions.rule: Art 354: modify (reduce/cancel) revenue distribution till end of financial year.

official_questions.stem: An official corresponding post to the Attorney General of India at the State level is
official_questions.core_fact: The Advocate General (Art 165) is the State counterpart of the Attorney General (Art 76).

statements.t: The State-level post corresponding to the Attorney General of India is the Government pleader.
The State-level post corresponding to the Attorney General of India is the Advocate General.
The State-level post corresponding to the Attorney General of India is the Amicus Curie.
The State-level post corresponding to the Attorney General of India is the Standing Counsel.

official_questions.rule: AG (Union, Art 76) - Advocate General (State, Art 165); Solicitor General is statutory.

official_questions.stem: All statements regarding the Roles/Functions/Responsibilities of the Finance Commission are correct, except
options: The Commission recommends sharing of net proceeds of taxes between the Centre and States
Recommending the principles for governing the grant-in-Aid to the States by the Centre
Recommendation on the matters referred to it by the President for the interest of sound Finance
Maintains the income and expenditure details of Centre and State Governments
official_questions.key: Maintains the income and expenditure details of Centre and State Governments
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 280(3): the FC recommends (a) distribution of net tax proceeds between Union and States and among States, (b) principles for grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of India, (c)/(bb) measures to augment State funds for local bodies, (d) any matter referred by the President in the interests of sound finance. It keeps no accounts.

statements.t: The Finance Commission recommends the sharing of net proceeds of taxes between the Centre and States.
The Finance Commission recommends the principles governing grants-in-aid to the States by the Centre.
The Finance Commission makes recommendations on matters referred to it by the President in the interests of sound finance.
statements.d: referred to it by the President

statements.t: The Finance Commission maintains the income and expenditure details of the Centre and State Governments.
statements.fact: The FC only recommends; accounts are kept by the Controller General of Accounts / Accountants General and audited by the CAG.

official_questions.rule: FC = recommends (Art. 280(3)); accounts = CGA/AG; audit = CAG.

official_questions.stem: Regarding the Election Commission of India, all following statements are correct, except
options: The members of Election Commission do not have equal powers with Chief Election Commissioner
Disputes related to the Election are not decided by the Election Commission only
The Election Commission of India enjoys Constitutional status
Keeping the voters list updated at all times is the responsibility of Elections Commission
official_questions.key: The members of Election Commission do not have equal powers with Chief Election Commissioner
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 324: ECI has constitutional status and superintends electoral rolls and elections. Under the 1991 Act the CEC and ECs have equal powers and decide by majority (T.N. Seshan v UoI, 1995). Election disputes go to the HC/SC by election petition, not the ECI.

statements.t: The members of the Election Commission do not have equal powers with the Chief Election Commissioner.
statements.fact: CEC and ECs have equal powers; decisions by majority (only removal protection differs).

statements.t: Disputes related to elections are not decided by the Election Commission alone.
statements.d: not decided by the Election Commission only

statements.t: The Election Commission of India enjoys constitutional status.
Keeping the voters' list updated at all times is the responsibility of the Election Commission.

official_questions.rule: ECI: equal powers + majority decisions; only CEC has SC-judge-like removal protection.

official_questions.stem: Locate the Constitutional power which enabled the Central government to Legislate on caw slaughter
options: Entry 17, list 3 in schedule for prevention of cruelty to animals
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 48 (DPSP) directs the State to prohibit slaughter of cows, calves and other milch and draught cattle. Legislative competence on preservation of stock is State List Entry 15; prevention of cruelty to animals is Concurrent List Entry 17 (basis of the Centre's 1960 Act and 2017 livestock-market rules).

statements.t: The Central government legislates on cow slaughter under its emergency powers.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: Emergency power is not the source; the key points to Art. 48.

statements.t: The Central government legislates on cow slaughter under Article 148.
The Central government legislates on cow slaughter under Entry 17, List III (prevention of cruelty to animals).
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: The key treats Art. 48 (DPSP) as the source.

statements.t: The constitutional provision enabling the Central government to legislate on cow slaughter is Article 48 of the Directive Principles.

official_questions.rule: Cow slaughter: Art. 48 (DPSP direction), Entry 15 List II (preservation of stock), Entry 17 List III (cruelty).
official_questions.key_note: Key kept. Caveat: a DPSP is not a source of legislative power; Central rules (2017) were framed under the PCA Act 1960 (Entry 17, List III), so option 3 is defensible. APPSC's key = Art. 48.

official_questions.stem: Among the following whose term of office is the longest?
official_questions.core_fact: CAG's term is six years or till age 65; President, Lok Sabha member and Vice-President have five-year terms.

statements.t: Among these, the longest term of office is that of the President.

official_questions.stem: The doctrine of "Paramountcy" is a legal principle:
options: to reconcile conflicting laws where both central government and Provincial governments have the power to create laws in relation to the same matter
To explain the law making authority of the Government
To provide law making authority to the Central government
To explain law making authority of the country
official_questions.key: to reconcile conflicting laws where both central government and Provincial governments have the power to create laws in relation to the same matter
official_questions.core_fact: Paramountcy reconciles conflicting central and provincial laws on the same matter, usually in favour of the central law (cf. Art 254).

statements.t: The doctrine of 'Paramountcy' is a legal principle to reconcile conflicting laws where both central government and Provincial governments have the power to create laws in relation to the same matter.
statements.d: to reconcile conflicting laws where both central government and Provincial governments have the power to create laws in relation to the same matter

statements.t: The doctrine of 'Paramountcy' is a legal principle To explain the law making authority of the Government.
statements.d: To explain the law making authority of the Government

statements.t: The doctrine of 'Paramountcy' is a legal principle To provide law making authority to the Central government.
statements.d: To provide law making authority to the Central government

statements.t: The doctrine of 'Paramountcy' is a legal principle To explain law making authority of the country.
statements.d: To explain law making authority of the country

official_questions.rule: Paramountcy/repugnancy = concurrent field; Art 254.

official_questions.stem: With regard to officers of All India Services, choose the correct answer from the following
options: A member of an all India Service can be dismissed or removed only by the Union government
A member of an all India service can be dismissed or removed by the State government also if he/she is serving under that State
In India, State government employees administer State laws only
Union government administer Union Laws through its Departments only
official_questions.key: A member of an all India Service can be dismissed or removed only by the Union government
official_questions.core_fact: An AIS member can be dismissed or removed only by the Union government (Art 311; AIS (D&A) Rules 1969); States administer Union laws too (Art 258A/256).

statements.t: With regard to All India Services: A member of an all India Service can be dismissed or removed only by the Union government.
statements.d: A member of an all India Service can be dismissed or removed only by the Union government

statements.t: With regard to All India Services: A member of an all India service can be dismissed or removed by the State government also if he/she is serving under that State.
statements.d: A member of an all India service can be dismissed or removed by the State government also if he/she is serving under that State

statements.t: With regard to All India Services: In India, State government employees administer State laws only.
statements.d: In India, State government employees administer State laws only

statements.t: With regard to All India Services: Union government administer Union Laws through its Departments only.
statements.d: Union government administer Union Laws through its Departments only

official_questions.rule: AIS: recruited and dismissed by Centre, serve States; 'only' statements need checking.

official_questions.stem: The subject of Education is included in:

official_questions.stem: Who appoints the Chairman of Finance Commission:
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 280(1): the President constitutes the Finance Commission every five years (or earlier), consisting of a Chairman and four other members whom he appoints; qualifications by the FC (Misc. Provisions) Act 1951.

statements.t: The Chairman of the Finance Commission is appointed by the President of India.

official_questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for Co-operation between the States:

official_questions.stem: Which of the following State in India first establish the Lokayuktha?
official_questions.core_fact: Maharashtra was the first State to establish a Lokayukta (Act 1971, office functional 1972); Odisha passed the first Act (1970) but the institution came only in 1983. AP's Lokayukta came in 1983.

statements.t: Maharashtra was the first State in India to establish the Lokayukta.

official_questions.rule: Lokayukta: first Act Odisha 1970, first institution Maharashtra 1971; term 'Lokpal/Lokayukta' by L.M. Singhvi (1963); ARC I recommended 1966.
official_questions.key_note: APPSC's revised key changed the answer to Maharashtra. Kept: Odisha had the first Act (1970) but the first functioning Lokayukta was Maharashtra's.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following subject comes under the Central Government:
official_questions.core_fact: Banking is Entry 45 of the Union List; agriculture (Entry 14), prisons (Entry 4), public health (Entry 6) are State List subjects.

statements.t: Banking is a subject that comes under the Central Government (Union List).

official_questions.rule: Union: banking, currency, defence, RBI; State: police, prisons, public health, agriculture; Concurrent: education, forests.

official_questions.stem: If the State fail to carry out directives of the Union Government, the President can-
official_questions.key: impose president rule on the State
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 365: where a State fails to comply with Union directions (Arts 256, 257), the President may hold that the State government cannot be carried on per the Constitution, allowing President's Rule under Art. 356.

statements.t: If a State fails to carry out the directives of the Union Government, the President can impose President's Rule on the State.

official_questions.rule: Directions (256/257) -> non-compliance -> Art. 365 presumption -> Art. 356 President's Rule (subject to S.R. Bommai 1994 review).

official_questions.stem: What are the rational aspects of Right to Information Act?

official_questions.key_note: Options not available; key 'All of these' kept.

official_questions.stem: Who was the first Loka Ayukta of Integrated State of Andhra Pradesh

official_questions.stem: The Chairman and other members of Union Public Service Commission shall be appointed by
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 316: the Chairman and members of the UPSC are appointed by the President (SPSC: by the Governor); removal only by the President (Art. 317).

official_questions.stem: Who is considered the highest Law Officer of India ?
official_questions.core_fact: The Attorney General (Art. 76), appointed by the President, is India's highest law officer; the Advocate General (Art. 165) is a State's law officer.

statements.t: The highest Law Officer of India is the Advocate General.
statements.fact: Advocate General is the State's highest law officer.

statements.t: The highest Law Officer of India is the Attorney General.

official_questions.rule: AG (Union, Art. 76) vs Advocate General (State, Art. 165); Solicitor General is statutory.

official_questions.stem: The Parliament is empowered to make any law for the whole or any part of India for the sake of implementing international treatise
options: With the consent of all the States
With the consent of the majority of States
With the consent of the State
Without the consent of any State
official_questions.key: Without the consent of any State
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 253: Parliament may make any law for the whole or any part of India for implementing any treaty, agreement or convention, even on State List subjects, without State consent.

statements.t: Parliament can legislate to implement international treaties with the consent of all the States.
statements.d: with the consent of all the States

statements.t: Parliament can legislate to implement international treaties with the consent of the majority of States.
statements.d: with the consent of the majority of States

official_questions.core_fact: Art. 266(1): all revenues, loans raised and loan repayments received by GoI form the Consolidated Fund of India; other public money goes to the Public Account (266(2)); Contingency Fund (Art. 267) is for unforeseen expenditure.

official_questions.stem:
The Parliament can make laws on subjects enumerated in the State list in the following conditions
A. On the request of two or more States.
B. The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution with at least two-thirds of the members present and voting, authorizing the Parliament to make laws on the subject in the national interest.
C. Proclamation of International Agreements.
D. The Lok Sabha passes a resolution with at least two-thirds of the members present and voting, authorizing the Parliament to make laws on the subject in the national interest.
official_questions.core_fact: Parliament may legislate on State List subjects: national interest on a Rajya Sabha resolution by 2/3 of members present and voting (Art. 249); national emergency (Art. 250); consent of two or more States (Art. 252); to implement international treaties/agreements (Art. 253); President's Rule (Art. 357). Lok Sabha has no such resolution power.

statements.t: Parliament can make laws on State List subjects on the request of two or more States.
Parliament can make laws on State List subjects when the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by two-thirds of members present and voting in the national interest.
Parliament can make laws on State List subjects to give effect to international agreements.
Parliament can make laws on State List subjects when the Lok Sabha passes a resolution with two-thirds of members present and voting in the national interest.
statements.fact: Only the Rajya Sabha (representing States) can pass the Art. 249 resolution.

official_questions.rule: RS special powers: Art. 249 (State List), Art. 312 (new AIS); both need 2/3 present and voting.

Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is not a correct explanation of (A)
official_questions.key: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is not a correct explanation of (A)
official_questions.core_fact: The UPSC (Art. 315) is the central recruiting agency of India and an independent constitutional body; its recruiting role flows from Art. 320 functions, not from its constitutional status as such.

statements.t: The UPSC is the central recruiting agency in India.
The UPSC is an independent recruiting constitutional body.
R explains A: being an independent constitutional body is why the UPSC is the central recruiting agency.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: Both are true, but constitutional status does not explain the recruiting function (Art. 320 does).

official_questions.rule: UPSC: recruitment (Art. 320) + independence (Arts 316-319); A-R on two features of one body is usually 'not the explanation'.

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following statements is/are correct ?
A. Residuary powers of legislation are included in Article 248 of the Constitution of India.
B. The Union Parliament has exclusive powers over any item not covered in the State or Concurrent Lists.
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 248 and Entry 97 of List I vest in Parliament exclusive power to make laws on any matter not in the State or Concurrent Lists, including taxes not mentioned there (residuary power - Canadian model).

statements.t: Residuary powers of legislation are included in Article 248 of the Constitution of India.
The Union Parliament has exclusive powers over any item not covered in the State or Concurrent Lists.

official_questions.rule: Residuary: Art. 248 + Entry 97 List I; courts decide whether a matter is residuary.

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true relating to Election Commission of India ?
A. The Election Commission of India is a three member Body.
B. The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India.
C. Election Commission of India is a Constitutional Body.
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 324: ECI is a constitutional body; multi-member (CEC + 2 ECs) since Oct 1993. The CEC and ECs are appointed by the President - since the CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act 2023 on a Selection Committee of PM, LoP and a Union Cabinet Minister (the CJI sat on the interim committee under Anoop Baranwal, Mar 2023).

statements.t: The Election Commission of India is a three-member body.
The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India.
statements.fact: The President appoints the CEC (on Selection Committee advice under the 2023 Act).

statements.t: The Election Commission of India is a Constitutional Body.

official_questions.rule: CEC: appointed by President on Selection Committee (PM, LoP, Cabinet Minister - 2023 Act); removal like SC judge.

a. NITI Aayog
b. National Commission for Minorities

official_questions.core_fact: Of the four, only the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (Art. 350B, 7th Amendment 1956) is constitutional; NITI Aayog is executive (Cabinet resolution 2015), NCM statutory (1992 Act), NHRC statutory (PHRA 1993).

statements.t: NITI Aayog is a Constitutional Body.
statements.fact: NITI Aayog is an executive (non-statutory) body.

statements.t: The National Commission for Minorities is a Constitutional Body.
The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is a Constitutional Body.
The National Human Rights Commission is a Constitutional Body.

official_questions.rule: Minorities: NCM statutory; Special Officer for LM constitutional (350B); NCSC/NCST/NCBC constitutional (338/338A/338B).

official_questions.stem: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Central Government to extend loans to State Governments ?
official_questions.core_fact: Article 293(2): the Government of India may make loans to any State (subject to Parliament's limits); Art 292 - borrowing by GoI; Art 294-295 - succession to property, assets, rights and liabilities.

statements.t: Article 292 empowers the Central Government to extend loans to States.
statements.fact: Article 292 deals with borrowing by the Government of India.

statements.t: Article 293 empowers the Central Government to extend loans to States.
Article 294 empowers the Central Government to extend loans to States.
statements.fact: Article 294 deals with succession to property, assets, rights and liabilities.

statements.t: Article 295 empowers the Central Government to extend loans to States.
statements.fact: Article 295 deals with succession to property in other cases.

official_questions.rule: 292 = Union borrowing; 293 = state borrowing + Union loans + consent for indebted states; 294-295 = succession.
